subject.title: fix(sms): ack rate-limited Twilio callbacks instead of dropping them [AI]

question: May the SMS webhook report successful delivery for a signature-validated callback that OpenClaw intentionally discards, or must HTTP success require processing admission or durable retention?
rationale: Source and provider behavior establish the tradeoff, but only the channel owner can define whether webhook success represents authentication, receipt, or accepted processing for OpenClaw's public SMS contract.

options.title: Require admission before success
options.body: Keep HTTP 429 unless the callback is dispatched or durably queued, preserving truthful delivery and overload signals.

options.title: Authorize ack-and-drop
options.body: Explicitly define HTTP 200 as authenticated receipt despite intentional loss, then document the contract and require live exact-head Twilio proof and monitoring guidance.

recommendation.title: Require admission before success
recommendation.body: Keep HTTP 429 unless the callback is dispatched or durably queued, preserving truthful delivery and overload signals.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work introduced the current callback-quota response contract being changed by this PR.
